title: Parallel and Cloud Computing
description: Making programs faster by running them on many cores, GPUs and machines — and running them on rented, scalable cloud infrastructure.
lecturer: Assoc Prof Dr Chan Huah Yong
outcomes: CO1 — Apply the concepts of parallel paradigm and cloud computing in the context of computational problem solving.
CO2 — Construct parallel programs using different parallel platforms and basic cloud services.
CO3 — Analyse issues in designing and developing parallel applications and cloud applications by using cloud services.

assessments.name: Assignment 1
assessments.detail: Group · given W3, due W9 · CO2 (build parallel programs)

assessments.name: Assignment 2
assessments.detail: Group · given W7, due W14 · CO1

assessments.name: Test 2
assessments.detail: 1 hour · in Week 14 · covers Weeks 9–12 topics · CO1

schedule.topic: Course Overview · Introduction to Parallel & Cloud Computing (HPC)
Introduction (cont.) · Cloud Computing and Related Technology
Parallel Architecture — Von Neumann to GPU, cache coherence, platforms
Parallel Program Basics — types of parallelism, overhead, performance measures
Communication in Distributed Systems — message passing, TCP/IP, RPC, RMI
Shared Memory Programming — threads, race conditions, Pthreads, mutex, semaphores
Pthreads & OpenMP — directives, reduction, performance
Mid-semester break
Virtualization — virtual machines, Docker
Container Orchestration — Kubernetes
GPU Programming — CUDA, OpenCL, OpenACC
Cloud Programming — Hadoop, MapReduce, HDFS
Cloud Service Models — IaaS, PaaS, SaaS
Cloud Architecture & Management — OpenStack, AWS, fault tolerance
Security in the Cloud

storyIntro: Hardware stopped getting faster on its own. So this course follows one thread: spread the work out (across cores, machines and the cloud) and then deal with every problem that spreading creates.

title: Software Process & Quality Assurance
description: How software is actually produced: modelling processes, life cycle models (waterfall to Scrum), managing and tailoring processes, and assuring quality.

schedule.topic: Topic 1 — Foundations
Topic 2 — Process definition & modelling (Part 1)
Topic 2 — Detailed-level modelling notations (Part 2)
Topic 3 — Software processes in the product life cycle
Topic 4 — Governance & management of software processes

topics: Topic 2 — Software Process Definition and Modelling

storyIntro: Software quality comes from the process that produces it. The course moves from writing a process down, to choosing its overall shape, to making an organisation actually follow it.
